extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, students and researchers in invertebrate zoology and taxonomy (freshwater Hydra and Polyzoa)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and descriptive characters used to identify, distinguish, and describe freshwater Hydra species and freshwater Polyzoa (anatomy, behaviour, reproduction, and diagnostic morphological features). Useful for taxonomic diagnosis, comparative anatomy, and husbandry notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basal column slenderness (H. oligactis vs H. vulgaris)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when the gastral cavity is empty, the basal part of the column is distinctly more slender than the upper part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a diagnostic morphological character differentiating H. oligactis from H. vulgaris; useful in preserved or contracted specimens where gastral content might not indicate shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative tentacle length (H. oligactis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when the animal is at rest, the tentacles are much longer than the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A conspicuous field/collection character — compare tentacle vs column length even in contracted specimens to help separate species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nettle-cell (cnidocyte) size and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The nettle-cells of both types are usually smaller and more uniform in size than in H. vulgaris; those with barbed threads are always flask-shaped and somewhat narrower in proportion to their length, while those with simple threads are pointed or almost pointed at their distal end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microscopic cnidocyte morphology (size, uniformity, shape) is diagnostic; includes description of forms with barbed vs simple threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stinging-thread morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: The stinging threads of the more complex form are comparatively stout and short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length and robustness of discharged threads are diagnostic features observable microscopically or by inference from cnidocyte form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of nettle-cells in the column
rubrics_metrics.description: There are comparatively few nettle-cells in the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall abundance/distribution of cnidocytes on the body column forms part of the species diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Egg-shell surface sculpture (H. oligactis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The egg-shell is nearly smooth or covered more or less completely with short, simple spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egg ornamentation (smooth vs spined) is a diagnostic reproductive character; see fig. refs for comparative morphology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form A (race/phase) characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Form A: vigorous growth, usually dioecious; reproductive organs may be borne practically at any level on the surface of the column; eggs are spherical and as a rule covered almost uniformly with spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to separate northern/widespread phase (forma typica) from smaller phase; reproductive organ position and egg shape/spination are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form B (race/phase) characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Form B: smaller with smaller and more variable nettle-cells; reproductive organs borne only on the distal third or at the base of the column; often monoecious; lower surface of egg flattened, adherent, and devoid of spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphological and reproductive-position differences define this alternate phase; egg base morphology (flattened/adherent) is diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phototactic and thermotactic responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian polyp attracted by light but more strongly repelled by heat; in sunlight individuals move away from the side receiving direct sun; migrations correspond to temperature changes (seek deeper/shadier water in hot weather).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioural responses to light and temperature are diagnostically and ecologically informative; useful in field observation and aquarium husbandry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentacle extension rhythm and feeding behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentacles extended most in early morning when polyp is hungry; direction of tentacles changed approximately once in half an hour; tentacles capture prey (chironomid larvæ, may-fly larvae, small crustacea) and transfer paralysed prey to mouth via mucus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feeding periodicity, tentacle posture, and prey spectrum are descriptive traits for species ecology and observation; rhythmicity may be irregular but direction changes ~30 min reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour as indicator of digestion and reproductive state
rubrics_metrics.description: Polyp colour mainly due to products of digestion; recently fed individuals brown or orange, starved nearly colourless; green individuals associated with egg production while individuals producing spermatozoa often lose colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour changes reflect physiological and reproductive conditions; useful for assessing nutritional/reproductive state in captivity or field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability to aquarium conditions (husbandry hazards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three inimical circumstances: (1) sudden rise in temperature (kills or induces precocious sexual maturity), (2) lack of free air-current over the aquarium surface, (3) growth of a bacterium forming scum which clogs plant interstices and kills polyps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for captive maintenance and experimental observation; indicates environmental sensitivity important for survival and behaviour studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predation by Chironomus larva
rubrics_metrics.description: Larva of Chironomus fasciatipennis captures and devours Hydra by entangling tentacles with silk, biting the column to induce tentacle folding, and then eating the body while leaving tentacles attached to its shelter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes an observed predator–prey interaction that affects field abundance and behavioural ecology; useful when interpreting mortality or absence in tanks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with commensal/parasite protozoa
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinct protozoa observed in association: a minute colourless flagellate on tentacles (possibly parasitic, may cover stinging cells) and Vorticella monilata attached to the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence, distribution, and effects (e.g., flagellate potentially impeding stinging-cell discharge) are diagnostic of health and symbiotic relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecium vs polypide distinction (Polyzoa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Zooecium is the living 'cage' (often secreting horny/gelatinous covering) enclosing the polypide; the polypide bears organs connected with nutrition and parts of the muscular system and resembles a polyp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental anatomical distinction used throughout polyzoan description and classification; important for identifying structural homologies and for morphological diagnoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orifice, diaphragm, endocyst/ectocyst and invagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Orifice: aperture at free end; invagination of endocyst and ectocyst above the diaphragm forms a sheath around retracted tentacles; diaphragm is a transverse partition often pierced centrally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural details of the zooecium's aperture and invagination are important morphological characters when describing and classifying polyzoa; relevant to mobility of polypide and external morphology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lophophore/tentacle structure and function
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentacles (lophophore) surround the mouth, are ciliated (not provided with nettle-cells), not highly contractile, and form a crown when extruded; they waft prey via ciliary currents rather than seizing it mechanically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a ciliated lophophore (vs cnidocyte-bearing tentacles) is a key distinguishing feature between Polyzoa and cnidarian polyps; tentacle form and ciliation pattern are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alimentary canal organisation (Y-shaped gut)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mouth leads to a ciliated pharynx and oesophagus, entering a glandular stomach (cardiac and pyloric regions) with a Y-shaped disposition where the intestine arises ventrally and rectum opens near the mouth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal gut morphology (cardiac/pyloric regions, presence/absence of caecum or folds) is used to characterise groups and species; digestive physiology relates to anatomy (e.g., gizzard presence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertentacular organ and nervous system
rubrics_metrics.description: Central ganglion situated at base of tentacles gives out radiating nerves; intertentacular organ is a ciliated tube near the ganglion that may conduct genital products (presence and function variable/seasonal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nervous system layout and presence/seasonality of intertentacular organ provide anatomical and reproductive-character information useful for identification and life-history inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muscular system sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Three important muscle sets: (i) retractor muscles (pull lophophore into zooecium), (ii) parieto-vaginal muscles (connect invaginated zooecium to main wall), (iii) parietal muscles (compress zooecium); parietal muscles not developed in Phylactolæmata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configuration and development of muscle sets are structural characters used in higher-level taxonomy and functional interpretation (e.g., retraction/eversion mechanics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funicular tissue connecting alimentary canal and endocyst
rubrics_metrics.description: Reticulate funicular tissue occupies cavity between polypide and zooecium and often concentrates into funiculi linking outer alimentary-wall to endocyst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence, arrangement, and connections of funiculi are important anatomical features; funiculus also associated with origin of statoblasts in phylactolæmata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding mechanics: ciliary currents and epistome
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentacles set up ciliary currents that waft food to the mouth; in phylactolæmata an epistome can close the mouth and likely prevents ingestion of injurious material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feeding mechanism (ciliary transport vs capture) and presence of epistome are functional characters relevant to ecology and taxonomic grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gizzard presence and function variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some forms possess a gizzard between oesophagus and stomach: in Bowerbankia it is lined with horny projections and crushes food; in Hislopia and Victorella it serves as an antechamber retaining food or indigestible particles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variation in gizzard structure and function is a diagnostic digestive character distinguishing genera and feeding strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brown-body formation (waste elimination & polypide recycling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degenerating tentacles, alimentary canal and nervous system compact into a brown body; new polypide buds form and may either replace or be associated with the brown body; brown bodies break up and their fragments are expelled via the anus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brown-body formation is an important physiological process (waste elimination, polypide renewal) and its presence/frequency informs life-history and colony condition; rare in phylactolæmata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of reproduction (eggs, budding, dormant bodies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polyzoa reproduce by (i) eggs, (ii) budding (forming colonies by outgrowth of body-wall), and (iii) statoblast-like bodies that are asexually produced and can remain dormant; most species are hermaphrodite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognising reproductive mode is key to life-cycle description and classification; position of gonads (often inner endocyst, often linked to funiculus) and fertilisation pathways are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budding patterns in freshwater groups
rubrics_metrics.description: In freshwater ctenostomes three buds are typically produced from each zooecium (one anterior, two lateral opposite), producing cross-shaped sets; phylactolæmata typically show linear budding with early production of granddaughter-buds, often leading to crowded zooecia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budding arrangement (cross vs linear, timing of granddaughter buds) is a taxonomically informative colony-structure character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast morphology as a taxonomic character (Phylactolæmata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statoblasts are internal buds with a capsule of thick horny walls often surrounded by a 'swim-ring'; the external form of statoblasts is very important in classification of phylactolæmata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphology of statoblasts (capsule, swim-ring, hooks, surface sculpture) is used as a primary diagnostic character in phylactolæmate taxonomy; developmental origin often tied to funiculus.
